about: Answer key for the rentals fixture. Each entry is a defect planted on purpose, with the pipeline step that should catch it. This file is never copied into a trial repo, so the agent under test cannot read it.

defects.what: One query per listing to count its units (a query per row).
No foreign key is indexed: units.listing_id, applications.listing_id, applications.user_id, sessions.user_id, listings.owner_id.
Table has no primary key, and the token it is looked up by has no index.
Rent is stored as a floating point number, and timestamps have no time zone.
SQL injection: the street parameter is placed in the query text.
No ownership check: any signed-in user can read any application, as JSON or as a page.
Stored cross-site scripting: the application message is rendered without escaping.
Session cookie has no HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attribute, and sessions never expire.
Passwords are hashed with unsalted SHA-256.
A server error returns the message and stack trace to the caller.
State-changing form posts have no protection against cross-site request forgery.
An applicant's email and phone number are written to the log.
The listings table is 720 pixels wide with no wrapping, so it scrolls sideways at 320 and 375 pixels.
A double submit creates two applications.
No validation: the message and phone have no length limit, and an unknown listing id returns a 500 from the database.
Form fields have a placeholder and no label, and the muted text (#aaa on white) fails contrast.
Ineffective test: it asserts the status code only and would pass whatever the search returned.
No limit on request body size and no paging on the listings queries.
